_comment: The worked example of a non-verbal pack: a figure declared as data, and answers that are pictures rather than words. Copy this shape. Every figure kind and every answer arrangement the build supports is here, and CI validates and imports it, so an example that drifts out of contract fails the build rather than teaching the drift to whoever copies it. The vocabulary these specs draw from is printed by `python3 elevenplus_data/preview_figures.py`. Some questions below use a named `template_id` instead of a hand-built `cells`/`cell` — see the Templates section of this folder's CLAUDE.md for the full list and what each one needs.

questions.stem: Which shape comes next in the series?
questions._note: The stem figure is the sequence with one cell left blank; `blank` names which, and that cell must be null. The answers are separate panels, one per option.

data.alt: A flag turning a quarter turn clockwise each time, with the fourth missing

options.text: flag, turned 270°, with a corner mark
flag, turned 90°, with a corner mark
flag, turned 180°, with a corner mark
flag, reflected horizontally, turned 270°, with a corner mark

questions.explanation: The flag turns a quarter turn clockwise each time: 0°, 90°, 180°, so the next is 270°.

questions.stem: Which shape is the odd one out?
questions._note: No stem figure at all: the options ARE the question. The rule is the number of sides, so every shape is drawn identically otherwise. Each option uses `nvr.odd_one_out`: a shared base cell (`common`) with the one field the rule turns on (`field`/`value`) overridden — the template's guarantee is that nothing else differs between options.

options.text: pentagon, hatch shading
hexagon, hatch shading
circle, hatch shading
octagon, hatch shading

questions.explanation: Every other shape is a polygon with straight sides. The circle has none, so it is the odd one out.

questions.stem: The first shape changes into the second in the same way the third changes into which option?
questions._note: `template_id` names the arrangement — a row of two pairs with a separator, one cell blank — so this question only supplies the three shapes that differ. `nvr.simple_analogy` resolves to the exact `nvr_grid`/`cells`/`blank`/`separator_after` shape this pattern always takes; see elevenplus_data/CLAUDE.md's Templates section for the full list.

data.alt: An L reflected, then a right-angled triangle, with its pair missing

options.text: right triangle, reflected horizontally
right triangle, turned 180°
right triangle, turned 90°
right triangle, solid shading

questions.explanation: The L is reflected left-to-right, not turned. Doing the same to the triangle gives the reflected triangle.

questions.stem: Each shape has a code. Which option is coded correctly?
questions._note: A 2x3 grid: `cols` sets the width and the cells run in reading order. `nvr.corner_code` builds a cell from a base shape plus a small marker at a named corner, so this question only lists the (shape, corner) pairs rather than each cell's full glyph list.

data.alt: Squares and triangles, each with a dot in one of three corners

options.text: hexagon with a dot in the top-left corner
hexagon with a dot in the bottom-right corner
hexagon with a dot in the centre
hexagon with three dots along the bottom

questions.explanation: The first letter of the code is the shape and the second is the corner the dot sits in. The top-left corner is the only one that matches.

questions.stem: Which of these nets folds up to make a cube?
questions._note: A net is a list of [row, column] squares. Each square is half a panel wide, so a net and a shape panel in the same paper are visibly the same scale.

options.text: a row of four squares with one above the second and one below the third
two rows of three squares
a row of four squares with two side by side above it
a column of four squares with two beside the top of it

questions.explanation: A strip of four faces with one face above and one below always folds into a cube. The others leave a face missing or two faces overlapping.
